subject: Public privacy help text for Hosted API & Console — Greenfield questions
messages:
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: privacy@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-07T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify Hosted API public language on data residency & subprocessors

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security/privacy team about public-facing language on your hosted API and the Console:

1) Data residency statement — we want a short, customer-facing sentence we can use in procurement docs that explains where customer data is stored and what controls exist.
2) Subprocessor notice — your DPA lists many subprocessors; we need a one-line explanation we can show non-technical stakeholders and a link to the full list.
3) Cross-border transfers — does your hosted API rely on transfers outside the EU/UK, and do you have standard contractual clauses or an alternative mechanism?

If you can send a short "help text" snippet we can paste into our internal evaluation notes (and a link to a public page), that would be ideal.

Regards,
Sam Ortiz
Senior Manager, InfoSec
Greenfield Health

Attachment: none

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-07T17:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Hosted API public language on data residency & subprocessors

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. I've drafted concise help-text options below for each ask; the goal was plain-language short bullets suitable for procurement or an FAQ. Please see the attached Word draft (draft_console_privacy_snippets_v2.docx) for alternate phrasings and the public link.

Proposed short snippets (pick one per bullet):

- Data residency (option A): "Customer data processed by Redwood Inference is stored in the region(s) selected by the customer; we offer hosted regions in the US and EU and can support dedicated or private deployments for localized storage."
- Data residency (option B, shorter): "Data is kept in the region you choose (US or EU). Private or dedicated deployments are available for stricter jurisdictional controls."

- Subprocessor notice (one-liner): "We use a small set of vetted subprocessors for hosting, monitoring, and payments — the full list and roles are published here: [link to subprocessor page]."

- Cross-border transfers (plain text): "Some hosted operations may involve transfers across borders; we rely on standard contractual clauses and other legal mechanisms and publish transfer details in our DPA."

Suggested placement: a short "Privacy & Data" callout on the Console onboarding page + an expandable FAQ entry in the public docs.

I've looped in Neha (privacy) and Kimberly (legal/product) to confirm legal accuracy and to attach the CSV of subprocessors. If this looks good to you, Marcus from Sales will use the concise lines in procurement emails.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_console_privacy_snippets_v2.docx

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T20:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Hosted API public language on data residency & subprocessors

Laura —

Thanks for the initial wording. A few edits to keep legal alignment and avoid overpromising:

- For the data residency lines, prefer the shorter option but add "where available" to avoid implying regions we don't yet host: "Data is kept in the region you choose (US or EU, where available)."
- Subprocessor one-liner: swap "small set" for "a limited set of subprocessors" and add a parenthetical: "(roles: hosting, monitoring, payments)."
- Cross-border transfers: replace "other legal mechanisms" with "supplementary safeguards where applicable" and reference SCCs explicitly for EU customers.

Suggested final help text (single compact paragraph we can surface in-app):

"Redwood processes customer data in the region(s) selected by customers (US or EU, where available). We engage a limited set of subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, payments); the full list and each subprocessor's role are published publicly. For EU customers, we use Standard Contractual Clauses and other applicable safeguards for cross-border transfers."

I attached the current subprocessor CSV so Sam's team can validate vendor names and purposes.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_subprocessor_list_2026.csv

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Hosted API public language on data residency & subprocessors

Sam —

Neha and Kimberly reviewed and we landed on a compact paragraph you can use in procurement notes or paste into an internal FAQ:

"Redwood processes customer data in the region(s) selected by customers (US or EU, where available). We engage a limited set of subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, payments); the full list and each subprocessor's role are published publicly. For EU customers, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses and supplementary safeguards where applicable for cross-border transfers."

Public link to subprocessor registry and the short FAQ draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3C-console-privacy-draft

If Greenfield needs anything tailored (e.g., contract language or more granular locality statements for specific environments), let us know and Neha's team can propose contract addenda.

Best,
Laura
